images.section_title: Introduction to Reading Signal Values from Graphs
images.image_description: Create a clean continuous-time signal graph on a coordinate plane. Label the horizontal axis \(t\) and the vertical axis \(x(t)\). Draw one simple signal curve or piecewise-linear signal that passes through the grid point \((2,3)\). Mark the time \(t_0=2\) on the horizontal axis, draw a vertical guide from \(t=2\) up to the signal, and draw a horizontal guide from that signal point to the vertical value \(x(t_0)=3\). Keep the plot uncluttered and instructional, with clear tick marks and no decorative elements.

images.section_title: Reading a Signal Value at a Marked Time

entries.lesson_core_move: Convert graphical or functional continuous-time signal descriptions into piecewise definitions by assigning each time interval its correct expression and boundary condition.

images.section_title: Writing a Piecewise Definition from Constant Graph Segments
images.image_description: Create a clean coordinate-plane plot of a continuous-time signal. Label the horizontal axis t and the vertical axis x(t). Show a horizontal segment at x(t)=3 from t=-2 inclusive to t=1 exclusive, and a horizontal segment at x(t)=-2 from t=1 inclusive to t=4 inclusive. Mark t-axis ticks at -2, 1, and 4, and mark y-axis levels 3 and -2. Use a closed dot at (-2,3), an open dot at (1,3), a closed dot at (1,-2), and a closed dot at (4,-2). Do not include sloped segments, curved segments, or decorative elements.
images.report: Horizontal segments at constant levels 3 and -2.; Open and closed circles at $t=1 show the interval split cleanly$.
images.lesson_core_move: Convert graphical or functional continuous-time signal descriptions into piecewise definitions by assigning each time interval its correct expression and boundary condition.

images.section_title: Writing a Piecewise Definition from Constant Graph Segments

Show a horizontal segment at x(t)=-1 from t=0 inclusive to t=2 exclusive, and a horizontal segment at x(t)=4 from t=2 inclusive to t=5 inclusive. Mark t-axis ticks at 0, 2, and 5, and mark y-axis levels -1 and 4. Use a closed dot at (0,-1), an open dot at (2,-1), a closed dot at (2,4), and a closed dot at (5,4). Do not include sloped segments, curved segments, or decorative elements.
images.report: Horizontal segments at -1 and 4 with a breakpoint at $t=2$.; The origin tick is shown because $t=0 is part of the prompt$.

entries.lesson_core_move: Classify a continuous-time signal from its graph or piecewise definition as even, odd, or neither by comparing $x(t)$ with $x(-t)$ over matching positive and negative time regions.

images.section_title: Introduction to Even and Odd Signal Symmetry
images.image_description: Create a compact coordinate-plane comparison figure with three side-by-side continuous-time signal sketches. Sketch 1 is labeled "even" and shows a simple piecewise-linear triangular pulse centered at \(t=0\), mirrored across the vertical axis, with matched points at \(t=-1\) and \(t=1\) highlighted at the same height. Sketch 2 is labeled "odd" and shows a simple piecewise-linear signal with origin symmetry, passing through the origin, with matched points at \(t=-1\) and \(t=1\) highlighted at equal magnitude and opposite signs. Sketch 3 is labeled "neither" and shows a simple piecewise-linear signal with a highlighted matched pair at \(t=-1\) and \(t=1\) whose heights are neither equal nor opposites. Label each horizontal axis \(t\) and each vertical axis \(x(t)\); use integer tick marks and minimal styling.
images.report: Three-panel comparison of even, odd, and neither symmetry.; Each panel uses the same axis scale with matched sample markers.
images.lesson_core_move: Classify a continuous-time signal from its graph or piecewise definition as even, odd, or neither by comparing \(x(t)\) with \(x(-t)\) over matching positive and negative time regions.

images.report: Question-prompt version of the even trapezoid.; Mirror symmetry is visible without a classification label.

images.section_title: Introduction to Basic Signal Parameters: Amplitude, Offset, and Duration
images.image_description: Create a clean continuous-time signal plot with horizontal axis labeled t and vertical axis labeled x(t). The signal should be zero outside a finite support interval and nonzero on one active interval. On the active portion, show a visible maximum level, visible minimum level, a center or baseline level, and the two support endpoints. Add simple instructional labels or markers for amplitude as a vertical distance from baseline to extremum, vertical offset as the baseline or center level, and duration as a horizontal bracket across the support interval. Use clear tick marks and avoid decorative details.
images.report: One annotated plot introduces amplitude, vertical offset, and duration together.; The baseline, amplitude, and duration are marked with compact A/C/D labels.
